assertion.prompt: Can the SARS-CoV-2 Nsp3 Mac1 macrodomain be controlled as a thermodynamic pivot point — by allosteric stabilization of distinct conformational states or by PROTAC-based physical degradation — to restore host PARP9/DTX3L-dependent antiviral ADP-ribosylation and arrest viral replication, and is this strategy broadly active across coronaviruses?
assertion.rationale:
The Nsp3 Mac1 macrodomain is a conserved, structurally tractable viral enzyme that selectively hydrolyzes the end product of the host IFN-PARP antiviral program. Active-site inhibitors target the ADP-ribose pocket directly, but the broader interactome framing suggests an alternative: stabilize defined conformational states of Mac1 with allosteric binders to test how each conformation reshapes the host PARP-mediated antiviral response, or eliminate the protein outright with a viral-protein-directed PROTAC warhead. Because Mac1 folds are conserved across SARS-CoV-2, SARS-CoV, and MERS-CoV, conformational stabilizers or degraders may have broad anti-coronavirus activity — the kind of pivot-point control that distinguishes a thermodynamic interactome framing from single-enzyme inhibition.
Both arms of the question are open at the level of chemical matter, not merely of biology. No allosteric site has been identified or characterized on any viral macrodomain; the only validated macrodomain allosteric ligand series remains GeA-69 against human PARP14 macrodomain 2, whose selectivity derives from PARP14-specific features. No Mac1-directed PROTAC has been designed, synthesized, or tested, and every published SARS-CoV-2 degrader targets a standalone viral protein rather than a domain embedded in the membrane-associated nsp3 polyprotein. The third CACHE challenge screened 1739 candidate ligands from 23 groups and returned only canonical adenine-mimetic orthosteric chemotypes, so community hit-finding has not yet produced a non-orthosteric starting point either.
The comparator arm has meanwhile moved. Active-site inhibition now has in vivo pharmacological proof of concept (AVI-4206) and an independent chemotype that represses coronavirus replication, and serial passage under that second chemotype has already produced a resistant Mac1 double mutant that is itself attenuated in mice. Allosteric or degradation-based control therefore has to demonstrate specific added value in breadth, resistance profile, or efficacy, not merely that it works.

proposed_experiments.name: Allosteric Mac1 conformational stabilization versus PROTAC degradation in SARS-CoV-2-infected airway organoids
proposed_experiments.description: Infect human airway organoids and ACE2/TMPRSS2-positive lung epithelial lines with authentic SARS-CoV-2 and treat with (a) active-site Mac1 inhibitors, (b) allosteric Mac1 binders tuned to stabilize discrete conformational states, and (c) a viral-Mac1-directed PROTAC warhead. Read out viral genome replication, infectious virus production, host PARP9/DTX3L-mediated ADP-ribosylation marks on host substrates, interferon-stimulated gene induction, and downstream cytokine and tissue-damage signatures. Repeat across SARS-CoV-2, SARS-CoV, and MERS-CoV Mac1 orthologs to test pan-coronavirus activity.

assertion.prompt: SARS-CoV-2 infection has been associated with both incident type 1 and type 2 diabetes, yet the mechanistic pathways and patient risk factors that predispose to one versus the other remain unclear. Do viral and/or host immune and metabolic pathways distinguish type 1 (autoimmune beta-cell destruction) from type 2 (insulin resistance + relative beta-cell inadequacy) post-COVID trajectories?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#SARS-CoV-2 Spike-Mediated Entry via ACE2 and TMPRSS2
assertion.rationale: Meta-analyses and prospective cohorts report increased incidence of both type 1 diabetes (especially in children with new-onset DKA above baseline) and type 2 diabetes (particularly in hospitalized and older adults). The role of SARS-CoV-2 as a direct trigger of autoimmunity, a driver of insulin resistance through persistent inflammation, or an unmasker of pre-existing glucose intolerance is not yet resolved. Mechanistic and genetic factors that predict which type develops are largely unknown.

selected_evidence.snippet: Soon, additional studies began to identify similar increases in new-onset type 2 diabetes [17].

assertion.prompt: Mac1-directed therapy works by lifting viral suppression of host ADP-ribosylation, so its benefit is predicted to depend on the patient's own interferon competence. Does a Mac1 inhibitor retain efficacy in the roughly one in five patients with critical COVID-19 who carry anti-type-I interferon autoantibodies or an inborn error of type I interferon immunity, and should interferon autoantibody status therefore be a companion diagnostic rather than an exclusion?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#RNA Virus-Induced Interferon and PARP Activation
assertion.rationale:
Every published Mac1 inhibitor whose mechanism has been dissected acts through immune restoration rather than through direct antiviral blockade, and in both compound series the cellular antiviral effect is explicitly interferon dependent. That makes host interferon competence a gate on the entire therapeutic strategy, and the gate is not hypothetical: inborn errors of type I interferon immunity account for 1 to 5 percent of unvaccinated patients with critical pneumonia and anti-interferon autoantibodies for another 15 to 20 percent, so the patients most likely to need a novel antiviral are enriched for the defect that would blunt it.
The gap is that this has never been tested. No Mac1 inhibitor has entered a clinical trial, so no cohort stratified by interferon autoantibody status or by interferon-stimulated gene score exists, and the preclinical interferon dependence has only been shown by adding or withholding interferon gamma in culture, not by comparing hosts that differ in endogenous type I interferon capacity. Resolving it needs either an animal model with defined type I interferon pathway loss treated with an active-site Mac1 inhibitor, or prospective collection of anti-interferon autoantibody status in any future trial. The answer bears directly on the Mac1 pivot hypothesis's claim of broad activity, because the limitation applies equally to active-site, allosteric, and degradation-based approaches.

assertion.prompt: What distinguishes acute hyperglycemia during COVID-19 hospitalization (stress-hyperglycemia) from persistent de novo diabetes development post-COVID? Do the pathways driving acute metabolic decompensation during infection differ mechanistically from those driving long-term beta-cell loss or insulin resistance post-infection?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#SARS-CoV-2 Spike-Mediated Entry via ACE2 and TMPRSS2
assertion.rationale: COVID-19 hospitalized patients frequently develop hyperglycemia (~50%), but the majority resolve it post-discharge. However, population cohort studies (OpenSAFELY, N3C) and registry data report incident diabetes cases years post-infection. The mechanism(s) linking acute infection-driven hyperglycemia to persistent diabetes risk is not clear: stress-hyperglycemia may unmask pre-existing insulin resistance that progresses to type 2 diabetes, acute direct infection of beta cells may cause lasting damage, or unresolved post-viral inflammation may sustain pathways months/years later. A prospective multi-timepoint mechanistic study is needed.

selected_evidence.snippet: stress- and treatment-induced hyperglycaemia is common in critical illness, occurring in approximately 50% of affected individuals. While often transient, these effects may unmask persistent metabolic dysfunction in individuals at risk of type 2 diabetes [36, 37].

value.prompt: Can the SARS-CoV-2 Nsp3 Mac1 macrodomain be controlled as a thermodynamic pivot point — by allosteric stabilization of distinct conformational states or by PROTAC-based physical degradation — to restore host PARP9/DTX3L-dependent antiviral ADP-ribosylation and arrest viral replication, and is this strategy broadly active across coronaviruses?
value.rationale:
The Nsp3 Mac1 macrodomain is a conserved, structurally tractable viral enzyme that selectively hydrolyzes the end product of the host IFN-PARP antiviral program. Active-site inhibitors target the ADP-ribose pocket directly, but the broader interactome framing suggests an alternative: stabilize defined conformational states of Mac1 with allosteric binders to test how each conformation reshapes the host PARP-mediated antiviral response, or eliminate the protein outright with a viral-protein-directed PROTAC warhead. Because Mac1 folds are conserved across SARS-CoV-2, SARS-CoV, and MERS-CoV, conformational stabilizers or degraders may have broad anti-coronavirus activity — the kind of pivot-point control that distinguishes a thermodynamic interactome framing from single-enzyme inhibition.
Both arms of the question are open at the level of chemical matter, not merely of biology. No allosteric site has been identified or characterized on any viral macrodomain; the only validated macrodomain allosteric ligand series remains GeA-69 against human PARP14 macrodomain 2, whose selectivity derives from PARP14-specific features. No Mac1-directed PROTAC has been designed, synthesized, or tested, and every published SARS-CoV-2 degrader targets a standalone viral protein rather than a domain embedded in the membrane-associated nsp3 polyprotein. The third CACHE challenge screened 1739 candidate ligands from 23 groups and returned only canonical adenine-mimetic orthosteric chemotypes, so community hit-finding has not yet produced a non-orthosteric starting point either.
The comparator arm has meanwhile moved. Active-site inhibition now has in vivo pharmacological proof of concept (AVI-4206) and an independent chemotype that represses coronavirus replication, and serial passage under that second chemotype has already produced a resistant Mac1 double mutant that is itself attenuated in mice. Allosteric or degradation-based control therefore has to demonstrate specific added value in breadth, resistance profile, or efficacy, not merely that it works.

assertion.name: Allosteric Mac1 conformational stabilization versus PROTAC degradation in SARS-CoV-2-infected airway organoids
assertion.description: Infect human airway organoids and ACE2/TMPRSS2-positive lung epithelial lines with authentic SARS-CoV-2 and treat with (a) active-site Mac1 inhibitors, (b) allosteric Mac1 binders tuned to stabilize discrete conformational states, and (c) a viral-Mac1-directed PROTAC warhead. Read out viral genome replication, infectious virus production, host PARP9/DTX3L-mediated ADP-ribosylation marks on host substrates, interferon-stimulated gene induction, and downstream cytokine and tissue-damage signatures. Repeat across SARS-CoV-2, SARS-CoV, and MERS-CoV Mac1 orthologs to test pan-coronavirus activity.

assertion.prompt: Does SARS-CoV-2 directly infect and damage pancreatic beta cells during acute COVID-19, or is acute hyperglycemia driven predominantly by systemic inflammation, HPA-axis stress, and metabolic dysregulation in peripheral insulin-sensitive tissues?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#SARS-CoV-2 Spike-Mediated Entry via ACE2 and TMPRSS2
assertion.rationale: Post-acute SARS-CoV-2 infection has been associated with new-onset diabetes, raising the mechanistic question of direct viral pancreatic tropism vs. systemic inflammation as the driver. A comprehensive post-pandemic review (Said et al. 2026, Diabetologia) identifies conflicting evidence on whether SARS-CoV-2 directly infects pancreatic beta cells during acute infection, or whether acute hyperglycemia and persistent metabolic dysfunction post-COVID result from HPA-axis stress, pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF, IL-6, IL-1beta), and reduced peripheral insulin sensitivity. This distinction is mechanistically consequential: direct beta-cell tropism could produce permanent damage and predict Type 1-like post-COVID diabetes, whereas inflammation-mediated dysfunction would predict reversible Type 2 hyperglycemia. Resolution of this branch informs the mechanistic link to post-COVID diabetes development modeled in Long_COVID entry.

selected_evidence.snippet: We summarise proposed pathophysiological mechanisms, including the effects of SARS-CoV-2 infection in the pancreas and on peripheral insulin-sensitive tissues. We review key meta-analyses assessing the association between COVID-19 and incident type 1 and type 2 diabetes and highlight strengths and weaknesses of the epidemiologic studies

assertion.prompt: Mac1-directed therapy works by lifting viral suppression of host ADP-ribosylation, so its benefit is predicted to depend on the patient's own interferon competence. Does a Mac1 inhibitor retain efficacy in the roughly one in five patients with critical COVID-19 who carry anti-type-I interferon autoantibodies or an inborn error of type I interferon immunity, and should interferon autoantibody status therefore be a companion diagnostic rather than an exclusion?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#RNA Virus-Induced Interferon and PARP Activation
assertion.rationale:
Every published Mac1 inhibitor whose mechanism has been dissected acts through immune restoration rather than through direct antiviral blockade, and in both compound series the cellular antiviral effect is explicitly interferon dependent. That makes host interferon competence a gate on the entire therapeutic strategy, and the gate is not hypothetical: inborn errors of type I interferon immunity account for 1 to 5 percent of unvaccinated patients with critical pneumonia and anti-interferon autoantibodies for another 15 to 20 percent, so the patients most likely to need a novel antiviral are enriched for the defect that would blunt it.
The gap is that this has never been tested. No Mac1 inhibitor has entered a clinical trial, so no cohort stratified by interferon autoantibody status or by interferon-stimulated gene score exists, and the preclinical interferon dependence has only been shown by adding or withholding interferon gamma in culture, not by comparing hosts that differ in endogenous type I interferon capacity. Resolving it needs either an animal model with defined type I interferon pathway loss treated with an active-site Mac1 inhibitor, or prospective collection of anti-interferon autoantibody status in any future trial. The answer bears directly on the Mac1 pivot hypothesis's claim of broad activity, because the limitation applies equally to active-site, allosteric, and degradation-based approaches.

selected_evidence.snippet: Standard cellular models indicate that AVI-4206 has high target engagement and can weakly inhibit viral replication in a gamma interferon- and Mac1 catalytic activity-dependent manner.

assertion.prompt: Why do CNS, gastrointestinal and lymphoid compartments transform preferentially in CMMRD when mismatch repair is absent from every tissue?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#Constitutional Microsatellite Instability and Mutator Phenotype
assertion.rationale: Constitutional instability is systemic, yet the tumour spectrum is not. Constitutional instability scores differ by tissue (gastrointestinal > blood > brain) and rise with age within an individual, so the tissue-specific transformation risk is not simply a function of measured instability. The determinants - proliferative index of the stem compartment, tissue-specific dependence on MMR versus backup pathways, immune surveillance, or the tissue-specific probability of acquiring the somatic POLE/POLD1 hit - have not been disentangled. Getting this right would sharpen surveillance intervals, which are currently uniform rather than risk-weighted by tissue.

proposed_experiments.name: Clone-resolved mutation burden across matched normal tissues in CMMRD
proposed_experiments.description: Measure somatic mutation burden and microsatellite indel load at single-cell or clone-resolved depth in matched normal brain, intestinal crypt and haematopoietic compartments from the same CMMRD individual, and test whether the compartment with the highest measured instability is the compartment that transforms first.

proposed_experiments.name: Longitudinal constitutional-instability scoring against organ of first cancer
proposed_experiments.description: Score constitutional genomic instability serially in blood and, where available, gastrointestinal tissue from a prospective CMMRD surveillance cohort, and test whether the instability trajectory predicts the organ and timing of the first cancer well enough to justify tissue-weighted rather than uniform surveillance intervals.

selected_evidence.snippet: In normal cells, MMRDness scores differed between tissues (GI > blood > brain), increased over time in the same individual, and revealed genotype-phenotype associations within the mismatch repair genes.

assertion.prompt: How much residual mismatch repair activity is compatible with an adult-onset, Lynch-like phenotype, and where does the CMMRD/Lynch management boundary fall for biallelic carriers of hypomorphic variants?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#Biallelic Germline Mismatch Repair Gene Inactivation
assertion.rationale: Late-onset CMMRD is currently recognised case by case, after constitutional MSI testing contradicts an assumed Lynch diagnosis. There is no calibrated relationship between residual repair activity and age at first cancer, so a biallelic carrier of two leaky variants cannot be assigned to a surveillance schedule on genotype. The two schedules differ substantially (annual brain MRI and gastrointestinal endoscopy from early childhood in CMMRD; adult gastrointestinal and gynaecological surveillance in Lynch), so the cost of guessing is high in both directions.

proposed_experiments.name: Calibration of residual mismatch repair activity against age at first cancer
proposed_experiments.description: Assay residual mismatch repair activity quantitatively across a series of candidate hypomorphic MMR variants (leaky splice and missense alleles) and correlate the measured activity with constitutional instability score and age at first cancer, to establish whether residual activity predicts the CMMRD-versus-Lynch management boundary.

proposed_experiments.name: Constitutional MSI screening of adults with biallelic MMR variants of uncertain significance
proposed_experiments.description: Systematically apply constitutional microsatellite instability testing to adult patients carrying biallelic or compound-heterozygous MMR variants of uncertain significance who are currently managed as Lynch syndrome, to estimate how often late-onset CMMRD is being missed.

selected_evidence.snippet: Individualised management of mono- and bi-allelic carriers of hypomorphic MMR variants is needed until we better characterise the associated phenotypes.

assertion.prompt: What accounts for the slow ocular saccades, intellectual disability, and growth retardation of the childhood-onset family, none of which has an established substrate in SPAX9?
assertion.rationale: All three features are reported only in the p.Lys19del family, which has never come to autopsy. In the family that was autopsied, the brainstem — which contains the burst-neuron circuitry that generates saccades — was explicitly free of neuronal loss and gliosis, so the usual brainstem explanation for slow saccades cannot simply be carried over to SPAX9. The childhood intellectual disability is equally unaccounted for: the frontal cortical neuronal loss found at autopsy was an acquired lesion in adults with cognitive decline, not a developmental one, and whether the vermian hypoplasia imaged in the childhood-onset family contributes to cognition has not been tested. No mechanism at all has been proposed for the growth retardation, and the Chp1 mouse and chp1 zebrafish were phenotyped on motor and cerebellar endpoints only. These phenotypes are left unconnected rather than attached to a plausible-sounding node.

proposed_experiments.name: Developmental and oculomotor phenotyping of a CHP1 knock-in model
proposed_experiments.description: Phenotype a p.Lys19del knock-in mouse for growth curves, cognitive performance, and brainstem oculomotor structures, with quantitative oculography in any living CHP1 patient, to establish whether these features are CHP1-dependent and where they arise.

selected_evidence.snippet: No neuronal loss or focal gliosis was observed in the other regions of the brainstem and cerebrum, except for moderate neuronal loss (Fig. 1g) and gliosis (Fig. 1h) in layers II and III of the frontal cortex.

assertion.prompt: Is the hearing loss of the p.Arg91Cys siblings a CHP1-dependent feature, given that the discovery authors predicted CHP1 patients would be protected from deafness?
assertion.rationale: Biallelic SLC9A1/NHE1 loss of function causes ataxia with sensorineural hearing loss (Lichtenstein-Knorr syndrome), which makes auditory involvement look mechanistically plausible on the CHP1-NHE1 axis. The CHP1 discovery authors predicted the opposite: that the residual NHE1 left by a hypomorphic CHP1 allele is enough to protect patients from the deafness and epilepsy of NHE1 disease, noting that neither the Chp1 nor the Nhe1 mouse is deaf. The later-onset family then reported hearing loss in both siblings, contradicting that prediction — while the childhood-onset family, which carries the more severely destabilizing allele, had no hearing loss, which is the wrong way round for a simple NHE1-dose model. Neither report characterizes the hearing loss audiometrically or distinguishes sensorineural from conductive, no CHP1 model has an auditory endpoint, and both affected siblings were in their late sixties or seventies at death (onset at 30 and 56 with disease durations of 36 and 20 years), so age-related hearing loss is not excluded. No causal edge is drawn to this phenotype for those reasons.

proposed_experiments.name: Auditory phenotyping across the CHP1 allelic series
proposed_experiments.description: Measure auditory brainstem responses and cochlear NHE1 expression in Chp1 hypomorphic and Nhe1-deficient mice, and obtain age-matched audiometry in any newly ascertained CHP1 patient, to test whether hearing loss tracks residual NHE1 rather than age.

selected_evidence.snippet: reduced NHE1 certainly leads to ataxia, but remaining levels are sufficient to protect patients with CHP1 mutations from epilepsy or deafness

assertion.prompt: Do the human CHP1 disease alleles act purely by destabilizing the protein, or do they also perturb the calcium-dependent CHP1-NHE1 interaction?
assertion.rationale: Neither p.Lys19del nor p.Arg91Cys lies in an EF-hand calcium-binding motif, which argues against a direct effect on calcium-dependent binding — but this reasoning is inferential. Biophysical work shows that calcium modulates CHP1 conformation and its interaction with the NHE1 CHP-binding domain, so a calcium-independent destabilization mechanism cannot be assumed without measuring the mutant proteins directly. Which mechanism applies matters for whether pharmacological chaperones or calcium-pathway modulation could be relevant.

proposed_experiments.name: Direct biophysical characterization of mutant CHP1-NHE1 binding
proposed_experiments.description: Measure calcium-dependent conformational change and CHP-binding-domain affinity for recombinant CHP1 p.Lys19del and p.Arg91Cys by isothermal titration calorimetry and fluorescent-probe hydrophobicity assay, alongside wild-type CHP1, to separate a stability defect from a binding defect.

selected_evidence.snippet: a direct role of these variants in the calcium-dependent interaction between CHP1 and NHE1 would appear to be unlikely

assertion.prompt: What is the anatomical substrate of the pyramidal signs in SPAX9, given that the only autopsied patients had pyramidal signs but no demonstrated corticospinal pathology?
assertion.rationale: Pyramidal involvement is what makes SPAX9 a spastic rather than a pure cerebellar ataxia: spastic paraparesis in the childhood-onset family, and Babinski signs tabulated in all four reported patients. Yet the neuropathological study of the two p.Arg91Cys siblings — who had pyramidal signs themselves — localized the degeneration to the cerebellum and the dorsal column pathway, described only gracile fasciculus fiber loss in the spinal cord, and explicitly found no neuronal loss or gliosis anywhere in the brainstem or cerebrum outside layers II-III of the frontal cortex. No corticospinal tract degeneration and no motor cortex involvement is reported anywhere in either paper, and the family with the most prominent pyramidal phenotype has never come to autopsy. The pyramidal phenotypes are therefore left unconnected in the pathograph on purpose: the entry has no CHP1-dependent corticospinal lesion to attach them to, and inferring one from the bedside signs would assert a mechanism neither source contains.

proposed_experiments.description: Examine the lateral corticospinal tracts at every spinal level and Betz cells in primary motor cortex in any future CHP1 autopsy; in living patients pair motor evoked potentials with diffusion imaging of the corticospinal tract; and trace the corticospinal projection in a CHP1 knock-in mouse, to establish whether the pyramidal signs reflect a corticospinal lesion or a cerebellar contribution to tone and reflexes.

assertion.prompt: Do the Chp1 mouse and chp1 zebrafish models capture the extracerebellar human phenotype of SPAX9?
assertion.rationale: Both models were validated on cerebellar and motor-axon endpoints: the vacillator mouse on Purkinje-cell axon degeneration and ataxia, the zebrafish morphant on movement defects, cerebellar hypoplasia, and motor axon abnormalities. Neither has been shown to reproduce the intellectual disability, frontal-cortical neuronal loss, dorsal-root-ganglion and dorsal-column degeneration, growth retardation, or premature ovarian insufficiency seen in patients. Mechanistic inferences drawn from these models therefore apply confidently only to the Purkinje-cell arm of the disease.

assertion.prompt: What is the anatomical substrate of the pyramidal signs in SPAX9, given that the only autopsied patients had pyramidal signs but no demonstrated corticospinal pathology?
assertion.rationale: Pyramidal involvement is what makes SPAX9 a spastic rather than a pure cerebellar ataxia: spastic paraparesis in the childhood-onset family, and Babinski signs tabulated in all four reported patients. Yet the neuropathological study of the two p.Arg91Cys siblings — who had pyramidal signs themselves — localized the degeneration to the cerebellum and the dorsal column pathway, described only gracile fasciculus fiber loss in the spinal cord, and explicitly found no neuronal loss or gliosis anywhere in the brainstem or cerebrum outside layers II-III of the frontal cortex. No corticospinal tract degeneration and no motor cortex involvement is reported anywhere in either paper, and the family with the most prominent pyramidal phenotype has never come to autopsy. The pyramidal phenotypes are therefore left unconnected in the pathograph on purpose: the entry has no CHP1-dependent corticospinal lesion to attach them to, and inferring one from the bedside signs would assert a mechanism neither source contains.

proposed_experiments.name: Targeted corticospinal assessment in CHP1 patients and models
proposed_experiments.description: Examine the lateral corticospinal tracts at every spinal level and Betz cells in primary motor cortex in any future CHP1 autopsy; in living patients pair motor evoked potentials with diffusion imaging of the corticospinal tract; and trace the corticospinal projection in a CHP1 knock-in mouse, to establish whether the pyramidal signs reflect a corticospinal lesion or a cerebellar contribution to tone and reflexes.

selected_evidence.snippet: The histopathologic features of the nervous system in patients 1 and 2 were quite similar, being characterized by marked degeneration of the cerebellum and dorsal column pathway.

assertion.prompt: Is perifollicular microinflammation and fibrosis a cause of follicular miniaturization, a cofactor that accelerates it, or a consequence of it?
assertion.rationale: Small and selected biopsy studies show inflammation and sheath remodeling associated with AGA, but do not establish temporal direction or a treatment-responsive causal pathway. In one 44-person minoxidil subset, regrowth was observed in 55% with significant inflammation versus 77% without, not a halving. Scarring fibrosing alopecia in a pattern distribution is an important differential diagnosis rather than proof that all nonscarring AGA inevitably progresses to follicular destruction.

assertion.prompt: Is female pattern hair loss androgen-dependent at all, and if so through the same dermal papilla mechanism as the male disease?
assertion.rationale: Androgen-related tissue differences and clinical responses do not establish identical mechanisms across all female-pattern populations. Most affected women have normal circulating androgens. The negative 1-mg finasteride trial in postmenopausal women is dose- and population-specific. A 2025 randomized spironolactone add-on pilot now exists, but primary hair-count differences were not significant and the study was small. Larger trials with prespecified endocrine and tissue strata are needed to identify who benefits and whether response is mediated by the same dermal-papilla pathways as in male-pattern disease.

proposed_experiments.name: Confirmatory stratified antiandrogen trial in female-pattern hair loss
proposed_experiments.description: A larger trial could use prespecified androgen-status and tissue-expression strata, standardized background therapy and blinded hair-density outcomes to test heterogeneity of response. This would extend, rather than precede, the small 2025 placebo-controlled adjunct trial.

selected_evidence.snippet: In contrast to its beneficial effects in men, finasteride did not improve hair growth in postmenopausal women with FPHL.

assertion.prompt: Does follicular SULT1A1 sulfotransferase activity predict the response to topical minoxidil, and could it be used to select patients or to rescue non-responders?
assertion.rationale: Follicular sulfotransferase activity is a candidate minoxidil-response biomarker. A 2015 study prospectively assayed 15 participants before topical treatment and reported 100% sensitivity and 71% specificity against a later photographic response classification. Its combined 70-person calculation gave a 95.9% negative predictive value assuming a 40% response prevalence. This is not universal test accuracy, an allele-specific loss-of-function result or evidence that assay-guided prescribing improves outcomes. Broader external validation and prospective clinical utility remain unresolved.

assertion.prompt: Is melorheostosis a manifestation of LEMD3 loss of function, or a separate disease that happens to look similar and occasionally co-occurs?
assertion.rationale:
The 2004 gene-discovery paper put melorheostosis in its title alongside osteopoikilosis and BOS, and that framing persisted for years. It was wrong as a general claim, and the correction matters both nosologically and therapeutically.
What is settled: (i) some individuals in LEMD3 kindreds do develop segmental cortical hyperostosis read as melorheostosis, and they carry the family's germline LEMD3 allele; (ii) patients with sporadic isolated melorheostosis - no osteopoikilosis, no family history - repeatedly test negative for germline LEMD3 variants, and negative for LEMD3 somatic mosaicism in lesional bone and skin; and (iii) most such patients instead carry a post-zygotic activating MAP2K1 variant confined to the affected bone, with mutant allele fractions of 1-34% and absent from contralateral unaffected bone and from blood. So sporadic melorheostosis is a somatic MEK1 mosaic disorder and is not BOS.
What is not settled is the LEMD3-associated form. Within a kindred the germline allele is shared by everyone, yet only one member develops the segmental lesion, so the genotype alone cannot be the explanation. The long-standing hypothesis is a somatic second hit at LEMD3 in the affected segment, but that has been looked for and not found. Whether the LEMD3-associated segmental lesion is mechanistically the same entity as MAP2K1 melorheostosis, or a distinct lesion that resembles it radiographically, is unresolved - the two are convergent at the level of "excess cortical bone in an asymmetric focal pattern" and have not been compared histologically within one study.
Curation consequence: this entry models the segmental hyperostosis as a within-syndrome node of hypothetical mechanism, keeps sporadic melorheostosis in differential_diagnoses rather than in the pathograph, and does not assert that LEMD3 causes melorheostosis in general.

selected_evidence.snippet: The activating mutations (Q56P, K57E and K57N) cluster tightly in the MEK1 negative regulatory domain.

assertion.prompt: LEMD3 is expressed in essentially every nucleated cell and the loss-of-function allele is present in every cell. Why are the lesions confined to bone and dermis, and why are they focal within those tissues rather than uniform?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#Dermal Fibroblast Elastin and Collagen Overproduction
assertion.rationale:
This is the central unexplained feature of the disease and it has two parts.
Tissue selectivity: a ubiquitous 50% reduction produces disease only where BMP and TGF-beta signalling sets matrix output - osteoblast lineage and dermal fibroblast. A plausible reading is that these are simply the tissues whose phenotype is most sensitive to SMAD dose, but that has not been tested; no BOS-specific transcriptomic, proteomic or single-cell dataset exists in any tissue.
Focality within a tissue: this is the harder half. Cultured fibroblasts from clinically uninvolved BOS skin already overproduce tropoelastin more than three-fold, so the cellular defect is present where there is no lesion, and something else decides where a nevus forms. The same puzzle applies in bone, where the sclerotic nodules occupy a small fraction of a uniformly haploinsufficient skeleton. Two candidate explanations are on the table and neither has been tested in BOS tissue: a somatic second event confined to the lesion (searched for in LEMD3 and not found), or a local modifier such as matrix stiffness - the LEMD3-SMAD2/3 interaction weakens as stiffness rises, which would make the haploinsufficient cell progressively less able to restrain TGF-beta in exactly the stiffening matrix it is building, a plausible focal positive-feedback loop.

selected_evidence.snippet: Using human lung biopsies, we observed that these nuclear and cytosolic interactions are also present in tissue and found that fibrotic tissues exhibit locally diminished and cytoplasmically shifted LEMD3-SMAD2/3 interactions, as noted in vitro

So sporadic melorheostosis is a somatic MEK1 mosaic disorder and is not BOS.
What is not settled is the LEMD3-associated form. Within a kindred the germline allele is shared by everyone, yet only one member develops the segmental lesion, so the genotype alone cannot be the explanation. The long-standing hypothesis is a somatic second hit at LEMD3 in the affected segment, but that has been looked for and not found. Whether the LEMD3-associated segmental lesion is mechanistically the same entity as MAP2K1 melorheostosis, or a distinct lesion that resembles it radiographically, is unresolved - the two are convergent at the level of "excess cortical bone in an asymmetric focal pattern" and have not been compared histologically within one study.
Curation consequence: this entry models the segmental hyperostosis as a within-syndrome node of hypothetical mechanism, keeps sporadic melorheostosis in differential_diagnoses rather than in the pathograph, and does not assert that LEMD3 causes melorheostosis in general.

assertion.prompt: Is cognitive delay part of Buschke-Ollendorff syndrome, or an artefact of ascertainment and of contiguous 12q14 deletions being counted as BOS?
assertion.rationale: A 2016 systematic review reported cognitive delays in 50% of its own single-centre cohort and in 17% of literature cases published from 2007 onwards, with none reported before 2007. That temporal pattern is the problem: it is exactly what reporting bias looks like, and 2007 is also roughly when microarray testing became routine, so cases with a contiguous 12q14 deletion - which removes HMGA2 and other neighbours and does cause developmental delay and short stature - would have begun entering the BOS literature. A single-child 2024 preprint describing intellectual disability adds nothing decisive. No cognitive phenotype is deliberately curated in this entry's phenotypes block on this evidence. Resolving it needs neurodevelopmental assessment of a molecularly defined cohort with contiguous deletions excluded by array.

selected_evidence.snippet: However, 50% of the cohort from HSC had cognitive delays, and only cases from 2007 onwards reported cognitive delays (the prevalence was 17% among those cases).

assertion.prompt: Heterozygous Lemd3 mice have the same allelic state as human patients and show no skeletal phenotype at all. Is murine bone genuinely insensitive to Lemd3 dosage, or was the phenotype missed?
assertion.rationale: Human LEMD3 haploinsufficiency reliably produces osteopoikilosis. The heterozygous Lemd3 gene-trap mouse, examined by radiography, quantitative micro-CT histomorphometry across eight structural parameters, and conventional histology, showed nothing. The mismatch is not evidence-absent - the experiment was done and was negative - it is a translational validity problem, and it is the reason no animal model of the human bone phenotype exists. Alternatives that would discriminate: whether murine bone simply tolerates a halved dose (a real species difference in SMAD dose sensitivity), whether the murine lesion requires a longer lifespan or a mechanical challenge to appear, or whether the gene-trap allele is hypomorphic rather than null and the effective dose reduction was smaller than in patients. Until this is resolved, mechanistic and therapeutic hypotheses about the human lesion cannot be tested in vivo; a conditional or knock-in allele in the osteoblast lineage, or a patient-derived iPSC osteoblast system, is the obvious next step.

proposed_experiments.name: Osteoblast-lineage conditional Lemd3 inactivation
proposed_experiments.description: Inactivate Lemd3 conditionally in the osteoblast/bone-lining lineage and age the animals, testing whether tissue-restricted and more complete loss produces focal sclerotic nodules that the germline heterozygote does not.
would_support: pathophysiology#Bone Lining Cell Activation and Modeling-Based Bone Formation
supporting_outcome: Discrete lamellar sclerotic nodules appear within trabecular bone on micro-CT, with modeling-based apposition and normal remodelling rate on dynamic histomorphometry, mirroring the human lesion.
refuting_outcome: No focal sclerosis develops even with complete lineage-restricted loss and ageing, which would move the explanation away from osteoblast-autonomous SMAD dose and toward a systemic or developmental requirement.

selected_evidence.snippet: To investigate whether the heterozygous gene-trapped mouse is a good model for osteopoikilosis in humans, we studied these mice radiologically with high-resolution micro-computed tomography (microCT) and histologically.

assertion.prompt: What causes Buschke-Ollendorff syndrome in families with an unambiguous osteocutaneous phenotype and no detectable LEMD3 coding variant?
assertion.rationale: At least one family with textbook BOS - father and son with nevus elasticus plus radiographic osteopoikilosis - has been sequenced across all LEMD3 exons and splice sites with no variant found. Candidate explanations that have not been excluded include a deep intronic or regulatory variant, a copy-number change missed by sequencing (deletion/duplication analysis was not routine at the time), and locus heterogeneity involving another component of the nuclear-envelope SMAD-terminating machinery. The practical consequence is already established: a negative LEMD3 test does not overturn a convincing phenotype.

selected_evidence.snippet: Although the clinical findings are diagnostic of Buschke-Ollendorf syndrome, analysis of the LEMD3 gene showed no exonic mutations.

treatments#Methotrexate therapy for refractory or severe disease
assertion.rationale: FUMHD management rests on heterogeneous single cases and small reviews with no controlled trials, so no regimen is proven by RCT-grade evidence and the tradeoff between immunosuppression and infectious mortality is unresolved. assertion.prompt: In fusion-positive ARMS, is immunotherapy resistance driven by a fusion/enhancer-imposed immune-cold chromatin state, antigen heterogeneity, cancer-associated fibroblast checkpoint/cytokine support, or a combined tumor-intrinsic and microenvironmental resistance state?
assertion.rationale: Recent immunotherapy and tumor-microenvironment papers make the gap more specific than "immunotherapy has not worked." CAR-T reviews identify limited clinical activity and hurdles such as antigen heterogeneity and immunosuppressive microenvironments; tumor-immune reviews connect PAX3:FOXO1 to reduced antigen presentation and immune infiltration; and a 2025 fusion-positive RMS fibroblast model shows immune-checkpoint and cyclophosphamide-resistance effects. With the fusion/enhancer node now explicit, the remaining gap is whether immune resistance is encoded in the tumor-cell chromatin state, imposed by CAF-supported microenvironmental signaling, or produced by both layers together.

Test CAR-T targets, checkpoint blockade, CXCR4 inhibition, CAF depletion, and fusion/enhancer perturbation to distinguish antigen-loss, tumor-intrinsic immune-cold chromatin, immune-exclusion, and fibroblast-mediated resistance mechanisms.

assertion.prompt: Which upstream or feedback-maintenance mechanism is required for the fusion-dependent regulatory program that produces the ARMS-specific open-chromatin signature, and can any chemical or genetic perturbation phenocopy acute fusion withdrawal at that assay readout?
assertion.rationale: Older work established PAX3::FOXO1 and PAX7::FOXO1 as molecular drivers, but a 2025 therapy review still notes that standard systemic therapy remains VAC despite decades of fusion knowledge. The disease model now makes the hidden middle explicit but should not treat open chromatin as a causal node: open chromatin is the observable readout of a fusion-dependent regulatory program. The causal candidates are upstream or feedback-maintenance mechanisms such as PAX-FOXO1 protein abundance, ETS1/KDM3A cofactor occupancy, and YOD1/N-Myc stabilization. HDAC3-SMARCA4-miR-27a is better treated as a chemotherapy-resistance branch, and FGFR4/FGF8 signaling is better treated as a downstream output or feedback-control test, unless perturbation proves that either one feeds back onto the regulatory program. Forward curation through 2024-2026 provides partial therapeutic handles for those layers, but does not yet establish which handle changes the disease-defining regulatory state rather than only improving a downstream phenotype in one model context.

proposed_experiments.name: ARMS regulatory-state dependency screen using open chromatin as readout
proposed_experiments.description: Define disease-specific open chromatin regions in matched FP-RMS models and use that signature as an assay readout, not as the causal mechanism. Perturb candidate causes of the fusion-dependent regulatory program first: acute PAX3-FOXO1 withdrawal, PAX3-FOXO1/ETS1 complex disruption, and YOD1 inhibition. Then use HDAC inhibition as a resistance-branch test under chemotherapy pressure and FGFR inhibition as a downstream-output control. Compare diagnostic-like, relapse-like, and chemotherapy-resistant states to determine which perturbation changes the regulatory-state readout and which only changes viability, signaling, or drug response downstream.

assertion.prompt: In fusion-positive ARMS, is immunotherapy resistance driven by a fusion/enhancer-imposed immune-cold chromatin state, antigen heterogeneity, cancer-associated fibroblast checkpoint/cytokine support, or a combined tumor-intrinsic and microenvironmental resistance state?
assertion.rationale: Recent immunotherapy and tumor-microenvironment papers make the gap more specific than "immunotherapy has not worked." CAR-T reviews identify limited clinical activity and hurdles such as antigen heterogeneity and immunosuppressive microenvironments; tumor-immune reviews connect PAX3:FOXO1 to reduced antigen presentation and immune infiltration; and a 2025 fusion-positive RMS fibroblast model shows immune-checkpoint and cyclophosphamide-resistance effects. With the fusion/enhancer node now explicit, the remaining gap is whether immune resistance is encoded in the tumor-cell chromatin state, imposed by CAF-supported microenvironmental signaling, or produced by both layers together.

value.prompt: Which upstream or feedback-maintenance mechanism is required for the fusion-dependent regulatory program that produces the ARMS-specific open-chromatin signature, and can any chemical or genetic perturbation phenocopy acute fusion withdrawal at that assay readout?
value.rationale: Older work established PAX3::FOXO1 and PAX7::FOXO1 as molecular drivers, but a 2025 therapy review still notes that standard systemic therapy remains VAC despite decades of fusion knowledge. The disease model now makes the hidden middle explicit but should not treat open chromatin as a causal node: open chromatin is the observable readout of a fusion-dependent regulatory program. The causal candidates are upstream or feedback-maintenance mechanisms such as PAX-FOXO1 protein abundance, ETS1/KDM3A cofactor occupancy, and YOD1/N-Myc stabilization. HDAC3-SMARCA4-miR-27a is better treated as a chemotherapy-resistance branch, and FGFR4/FGF8 signaling is better treated as a downstream output or feedback-control test, unless perturbation proves that either one feeds back onto the regulatory program. Forward curation through 2024-2026 provides partial therapeutic handles for those layers, but does not yet establish which handle changes the disease-defining regulatory state rather than only improving a downstream phenotype in one model context.

assertion.name: ARMS regulatory-state dependency screen using open chromatin as readout
assertion.description: Define disease-specific open chromatin regions in matched FP-RMS models and use that signature as an assay readout, not as the causal mechanism. Perturb candidate causes of the fusion-dependent regulatory program first: acute PAX3-FOXO1 withdrawal, PAX3-FOXO1/ETS1 complex disruption, and YOD1 inhibition. Then use HDAC inhibition as a resistance-branch test under chemotherapy pressure and FGFR inhibition as a downstream-output control. Compare diagnostic-like, relapse-like, and chemotherapy-resistant states to determine which perturbation changes the regulatory-state readout and which only changes viability, signaling, or drug response downstream.

assertion.prompt: Which fusion-positive ARMS tumors have disease-specific open chromatin at FGF8 regulatory elements that correspond to previously reported PAX3-FOXO1/ETS1/KDM3A-bound enhancers of FGF8, and also show high FGF8 RNA, high FGFR4 RNA, and FGFR4 phosphorylation, such that the tumor is clinically responsive to FGFR inhibition? Conversely, which tumors express some of the FGF8/FGFR4/FGFR4_pY signature but are not FGFR-dependent because downstream RAS/PI3K activation, relapse-associated adaptation, or other resistance circuitry bypasses FGFR signaling?
assertion.rationale: Recent 2026 multiplatform profiling provides the strongest forward evidence that FGFR4/FGF8 coexpression with FGFR4 phosphorylation can identify FGFR-inhibitor-sensitive FP-RMS. The same paper frames the broader unresolved question: RNA overexpression alone is common, but it is not always clear when receptor expression marks kinase activation, signaling dependence, and drug response. Because the pathograph now connects FGF8 to the ETS1/KDM3A/PAX-FOXO1 chromatin cofactor module, the open curation problem is whether disease-specific open chromatin at FGF8 regulatory elements that correspond to PAX3-FOXO1/ETS1/KDM3A-bound enhancers of FGF8, direct factor-occupancy evidence where available, FGF8/FGFR4 transcript abundance, FGFR4 phosphorylation, and drug response form one coherent dependency signature or split into bypass states.

value.prompt: In fusion-positive ARMS, is immunotherapy resistance driven by a fusion/enhancer-imposed immune-cold chromatin state, antigen heterogeneity, cancer-associated fibroblast checkpoint/cytokine support, or a combined tumor-intrinsic and microenvironmental resistance state?
value.rationale: Recent immunotherapy and tumor-microenvironment papers make the gap more specific than "immunotherapy has not worked." CAR-T reviews identify limited clinical activity and hurdles such as antigen heterogeneity and immunosuppressive microenvironments; tumor-immune reviews connect PAX3:FOXO1 to reduced antigen presentation and immune infiltration; and a 2025 fusion-positive RMS fibroblast model shows immune-checkpoint and cyclophosphamide-resistance effects. assertion.prompt: Which upstream or feedback-maintenance mechanism is required for the fusion-dependent regulatory program that produces the ARMS-specific open-chromatin signature, and can any chemical or genetic perturbation phenocopy acute fusion withdrawal at that assay readout?
assertion.rationale: Older work established PAX3::FOXO1 and PAX7::FOXO1 as molecular drivers, but a 2025 therapy review still notes that standard systemic therapy remains VAC despite decades of fusion knowledge. The disease model now makes the hidden middle explicit but should not treat open chromatin as a causal node: open chromatin is the observable readout of a fusion-dependent regulatory program. The causal candidates are upstream or feedback-maintenance mechanisms such as PAX-FOXO1 protein abundance, ETS1/KDM3A cofactor occupancy, and YOD1/N-Myc stabilization. HDAC3-SMARCA4-miR-27a is better treated as a chemotherapy-resistance branch, and FGFR4/FGF8 signaling is better treated as a downstream output or feedback-control test, unless perturbation proves that either one feeds back onto the regulatory program. Forward curation through 2024-2026 provides partial therapeutic handles for those layers, but does not yet establish which handle changes the disease-defining regulatory state rather than only improving a downstream phenotype in one model context.

proposed_experiments.name: ARMS regulatory-state dependency screen using open chromatin as readout
proposed_experiments.description: Define disease-specific open chromatin regions in matched FP-RMS models and use that signature as an assay readout, not as the causal mechanism. Perturb candidate causes of the fusion-dependent regulatory program first: acute PAX3-FOXO1 withdrawal, PAX3-FOXO1/ETS1 complex disruption, and YOD1 inhibition. Then use HDAC inhibition as a resistance-branch test under chemotherapy pressure and FGFR inhibition as a downstream-output control. Compare diagnostic-like, relapse-like, and chemotherapy-resistant states to determine which perturbation changes the regulatory-state readout and which only changes viability, signaling, or drug response downstream.

assertion.prompt: Which achondroplasia features depend on the MAPK arm, which on the STAT1 arm, and what weight should the p38 branch carry, given that the only approved and late-stage drugs act on one arm?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#Prolonged FGFR3 signaling in growth-plate chondrocytes
assertion.rationale: Mouse genetics separates the arms — CNP overexpression corrects matrix synthesis through MAPK without touching STAT1, constitutively active MEK1 causes Stat1-independent dwarfism — and a CDK8 inhibitor now moves the STAT1-Ser727 branch in a mouse model without affecting MAPK activation. No study has tested the two interventions together, and no human data assign specific clinical features to specific arms; the vosoritide result is consistent with the model but does not rank the arms against each other. A third, p38 branch is proposed on the strength of a single ATDC5 cell-line study and is not curated as a pathophysiology node here for that reason.

proposed_experiments.description: Treat humanized FGFR3 p.Gly380Arg knock-in mice with a CNP analogue alone, a CDK8 inhibitor alone, both together, and vehicle, then compare long-bone length, growth-plate zone architecture, and phospho-STAT1 Ser727 versus phospho-ERK in the growth plate.

readouts.interpretation: A more-than-additive effect of the two agents would indicate that the arms contribute separably to the growth deficit.

refuting_outcome: Combined treatment matches the better single agent, indicating the arms converge on a shared limiting step rather than acting separably.

assertion.prompt: How much of the human growth-plate phenotype is attributable to the ciliary branch, as opposed to the direct MAPK and STAT arms it lies downstream of?

assertion.rationale: Cilium shortening and IFT20 mis-sorting are reproducible in chondrocytes from human achondroplasia and thanatophoric dysplasia cartilage and in mouse models, and a ciliogenesis-restoring compound increases bone elongation in the mouse. What has not been done is a measurement that separates the ciliary contribution from the receptor's direct signaling output: every available intervention acts upstream of both, and the rescue compound is not cilia-selective. Until such an experiment exists, the "achondroplasia is a ciliopathy" reading found in the source literature is an interpretive proposal rather than an established classification, and this entry curates the branch without adopting that label.

assertion.prompt: If statins do not act on FGFR signaling in cartilage, what mechanism accounts for the previously reported statin rescue of FGFR3-related chondrodysplasia?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#Prolonged FGFR3 signaling in growth-plate chondrocytes
assertion.rationale: A dedicated study found no effect of four statins on FGFR3 protein levels or on FGFR-mediated growth arrest, matrix loss, senescence, or hypertrophic differentiation across chondrocyte lines, embryonic tibia cultures, and limb-bud micromasses. That result narrows the earlier rescue reports: it rules out a chondrocyte-intrinsic FGFR mechanism, but it does not exclude an indirect or systemic effect, so statins are recorded here as an unresolved question rather than as a refuted therapy outright. No statin treatment entry is curated for this disease.
assertion.notes: Corresponds to gap KG-7 in the OpenScientist report for this hypothesis.

selected_evidence.snippet: We conclude that statins do not inhibit the FGFR signaling in chondrocytes. Therefore the statin-mediated rescue of FGFR3-related chondrodysplasia, described before, is likely not intrinsic to the growth plate cartilage.

assertion.prompt: By what mechanism does loss of a nuclear DNA-repair enzyme lower serum albumin and raise total cholesterol, and why do these markers appear only late?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#Persistence of Abortive DNA Ligation Intermediates
assertion.rationale:
Hypoalbuminaemia is written into the disease's own MONDO and OMIM labels, yet none of the references read for this entry offers a mechanism. Every source treats it as an association: the 2001 gene papers report it as a clinical characteristic, the 2003 French series and the 2011 Italian series quantify it, and the 2008 report places it in the adult stage. The searches run for this entry found nothing addressing the causal step, so the pathograph deliberately does not connect it to the APTX lesion by an edge.
The gap is worth stating rather than papering over, because dismech now also holds an entry in which hypoalbuminaemia *is* mechanistically explained - hypercatabolic hypoproteinaemia, where FcRn salvage failure raises the catabolic rate of albumin. A protein-turnover study in AOA1 of the kind Waldmann and Terry performed in 1968 would settle in one experiment whether the albumin here is under-synthesised or over-catabolised, and nothing in the literature curated here reports one.
Management practice has quietly taken a side. The published recommendation is a high-protein diet to prevent oedema by restoring serum albumin - which only makes sense if the albumin is substrate-limited, that is, a synthesis or intake problem. If AOA1 hypoalbuminaemia were catabolic in the way hypercatabolic hypoproteinaemia's is, eating more protein would raise the flux through a leak rather than fix it, and the FcRn disease is the demonstration: those patients synthesise albumin at a normal rate and are still hypoalbuminaemic.
So the assumption is testable and, so far as the literature read here goes, untested. It is also not idle: it is the stated rationale of a dietary recommendation given to patients.

proposed_experiments.name: Radiolabelled albumin turnover study in AOA1
proposed_experiments.description: Measure albumin synthetic rate and fractional catabolic rate in mutation-confirmed AOA1 patients with hypoalbuminaemia, with urinary and faecal protein loss excluded, to distinguish reduced hepatic synthesis from accelerated catabolism.

proposed_experiments.name: Serum albumin response to protein intake in AOA1
proposed_experiments.description: Measure serum albumin before and during a defined high-protein intake in AOA1 patients, to test the assumption embedded in the current dietary recommendation. A response supports a substrate-limited mechanism; no response, with normal renal and enteric protein handling, points at catabolism and would make the diet advice mechanistically wrong even if harmless.

selected_evidence.snippet: AOA1 is also characterized by axonal motor neuropathy and the later decrease of serum albumin levels and elevation of total cholesterol.

assertion.prompt: Why do the two natural-history sources report different mean ages of onset for AOA1, and which should a clinician use?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#Progressive Cerebellar Ataxia and Oculomotor Apraxia
assertion.rationale:
The GeneReviews chapter gives a mean onset of 4.3 years with a range of 2 to 10. The French series gives 6.8 plus or minus 4.8 years with a range of 2 to 18. The lower bound agrees; the upper bound differs by eight years.
The likely explanation is ascertainment rather than disagreement. The French figure comes from screening a referred series of 158 non-Friedreich recessive ataxia families, which will include patients who presented late enough to be mistaken for something else; the GeneReviews figure describes the disease as characterised in dedicated AOA1 series. A referral-based denominator shifts a mean onset upward and widens the range in exactly this way.
Both are recorded rather than averaged. For counselling, the wider range is the safer one: a first presentation at fifteen does not exclude AOA1.

selected_evidence.snippet: The first manifestation is progressive gait imbalance (mean age of onset: 4.3 years; range: 2-10 years), followed by dysarthria, then upper-limb dysmetria with mild intention tremor.

assertion.prompt: Should AOA1 be curated as a secondary coenzyme Q10 deficiency, and does coenzyme Q10 supplementation have a mechanistic rationale in this disease?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#Accumulation of Unrepaired Single-Strand Breaks in Post-Mitotic Neurons
assertion.rationale:
AOA1 has been discussed alongside the secondary coenzyme Q10 deficiencies, which would give it a mitochondrial arm and a supplement with a rationale. The one series in this entry's reference set that actually measured it found normal coenzyme Q10 in muscle, fibroblasts and plasma in five of six mutation-positive subjects.
That is a small number and a negative result, so it does not close the question. It is enough, though, to keep a mitochondrial node out of this pathograph: there is no measured coenzyme Q10 deficit to build one on, and inventing the node would create a therapeutic rationale the data do not support.

assertion.prompt: Is cognitive impairment universal in AOA1, or does intellect remain normal in a subset of patients?
assertion.rationale:
Two sources make incompatible universal claims. The 14-patient French series states that cognitive impairment was always present. The GeneReviews chapter states that intellect remains normal in some individuals, with varying degrees of impairment in others.
Both cannot be right as stated, and the disagreement is not resolvable from the abstracts curated here because neither reports the instrument used. "Cognitive impairment" assessed by formal neuropsychological battery and "intellect remains normal" assessed clinically can coexist in the same population: a patient with normal measured IQ and impaired executive or processing-speed performance would be counted in both categories by the two sources. Cerebellar cognitive-affective changes are exactly the kind that a global intellect judgement misses.
The phenotype band was lowered from OBLIGATE to FREQUENT rather than picking a winner, because a band should not assert more than the weaker of two conflicting sources allows.
A caveat on weighting: the GeneReviews chapter is formally retired and its own header warns the information may be out of date, so it is not automatically the better source. It is, however, the only one of the two that reports the observation prospectively across the disease's described natural history rather than in one ascertained cohort.

proposed_experiments.name: Formal neuropsychological profiling in a mutation-confirmed AOA1 cohort
proposed_experiments.description: Administer a battery separating global intellectual ability from executive function, processing speed and the cerebellar cognitive-affective domains, in mutation-confirmed patients stratified by disease duration, to establish whether the disagreement is about prevalence or about which construct is being measured.

selected_evidence.snippet: Intellect remains normal in some individuals; in others, different degrees of cognitive impairment have been observed.

assertion.prompt: By what mechanism does loss of a nuclear DNA-repair enzyme lower serum albumin and raise total cholesterol, and why do these markers appear only late?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#Persistence of Abortive DNA Ligation Intermediates
assertion.rationale:
Hypoalbuminaemia is written into the disease's own MONDO and OMIM labels, yet none of the references read for this entry offers a mechanism. Every source treats it as an association: the 2001 gene papers report it as a clinical characteristic, the 2003 French series and the 2011 Italian series quantify it, and the 2008 report places it in the adult stage. The searches run for this entry found nothing addressing the causal step, so the pathograph deliberately does not connect it to the APTX lesion by an edge.
The gap is worth stating rather than papering over, because dismech now also holds an entry in which hypoalbuminaemia *is* mechanistically explained - hypercatabolic hypoproteinaemia, where FcRn salvage failure raises the catabolic rate of albumin. A protein-turnover study in AOA1 of the kind Waldmann and Terry performed in 1968 would settle in one experiment whether the albumin here is under-synthesised or over-catabolised, and nothing in the literature curated here reports one.
Management practice has quietly taken a side. The published recommendation is a high-protein diet to prevent oedema by restoring serum albumin - which only makes sense if the albumin is substrate-limited, that is, a synthesis or intake problem. If AOA1 hypoalbuminaemia were catabolic in the way hypercatabolic hypoproteinaemia's is, eating more protein would raise the flux through a leak rather than fix it, and the FcRn disease is the demonstration: those patients synthesise albumin at a normal rate and are still hypoalbuminaemic.
So the assumption is testable and, so far as the literature read here goes, untested. It is also not idle: it is the stated rationale of a dietary recommendation given to patients.

proposed_experiments.name: Radiolabelled albumin turnover study in AOA1
proposed_experiments.description: Measure albumin synthetic rate and fractional catabolic rate in mutation-confirmed AOA1 patients with hypoalbuminaemia, with urinary and faecal protein loss excluded, to distinguish reduced hepatic synthesis from accelerated catabolism.

proposed_experiments.name: Serum albumin response to protein intake in AOA1
proposed_experiments.description: Measure serum albumin before and during a defined high-protein intake in AOA1 patients, to test the assumption embedded in the current dietary recommendation. A response supports a substrate-limited mechanism; no response, with normal renal and enteric protein handling, points at catabolism and would make the diet advice mechanistically wrong even if harmless.

selected_evidence.snippet: Prevention of secondary complications: High-protein diet to prevent edema by restoring serum albumin concentration; low-cholesterol diet.

assertion.prompt: Does the AOA1 phenotype vary with the APTX allele, or is it homogeneous regardless of mutation type and position?
assertion.rationale:
Two large series disagree. The 2003 French series singles out A198V as producing a remarkably severe and persistent chorea, against the usual pattern in which chorea fades. The 2011 Italian series states flatly that the phenotype was homogeneous irrespective of mutation type and location.
The disagreement may be smaller than it looks: A198V does not appear among the alleles reported in the Italian cohort, which found W279X, W279R and P206L homozygotes plus three novel truncating variants. A series that never observed the allele cannot contradict a claim about it. Recorded as a controversy rather than resolved in either direction, because settling it needs a cohort carrying A198V and scored for chorea persistence, which neither series is.

selected_evidence.snippet: The clinical phenotype was homogeneous, irrespectively of the type and location of the APTX mutation

assertion.prompt: Is PTCD3 deficiency a cause of Leigh syndrome, or of a Leigh-like syndrome that does not meet the diagnostic criteria?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#Subacute Necrotizing Degeneration of Basal Ganglia and Thalamus
assertion.rationale:
The founding 2019 report diagnosed its patient with Leigh syndrome. A letter in the same journal argued the imaging and clinical picture met criteria only for a Leigh-like syndrome. The 2023 series then titled itself "Leigh syndrome is the main clinical characteristic of PTCD3 deficiency" and set out to settle the question in favour of Leigh syndrome; the 2024 report nonetheless describes its own severe patient as Leigh-like, and its two adult patients as neither.
This entry does not adjudicate. It records the position of each report and keeps the pathophysiology node named for the lesion (necrotizing degeneration of basal ganglia and thalamus) rather than for either syndrome label, so that the mechanism does not inherit the dispute.
This entry quotes the 2023 series' summary of the challenge rather than the challenging Letter itself. The reason is recorded in the entry notes.

selected_evidence.snippet: These clinical manifestations align with a Leigh‐like syndrome.

assertion.prompt: Why do the optic nerve and the basal ganglia and thalamus degenerate when the translation defect is present in every cell?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#Subacute Necrotizing Degeneration of Basal Ganglia and Thalamus
assertion.rationale:
PTCD3 is expressed in all tissues and the mitoribosome is required in all of them, yet the disease is focal: the optic nerve in essentially every patient, the basal ganglia and thalamus in the severe pole, the peripheral nerve in several, and almost nothing else. Cardiac, hepatic and renal involvement, which is common across the mitoribosomal protein disorders as a class, has been minimal in these patients.
The only explanation offered is a general one - that retinal ganglion cells are especially vulnerable to defects in mitochondrial gene expression - and it is asserted rather than tested in PTCD3. It also does not address the basal-ganglia selectivity, which is shared with more than 75 unrelated Leigh-syndrome genes and is unexplained for all of them. The two selectivities may not have the same cause, and nothing in the PTCD3 literature distinguishes them.
This is recorded as a gap rather than a controversy because no source argues the other side; the question has not been addressed.

selected_evidence.snippet: Defects in mitochondrial replication, RNA transcription and translation initiate early‐onset optic atrophy, as these cells are highly vulnerable to mitochondrial dysfunction.

assertion.prompt: The only published whole-organism PTCD3 model is a lethal Drosophila null. Does any available model reproduce the human disease, in which every reported genotype retains residual protein?
assertion.rationale:
Evidence exists in a model system, and its translational validity is the open question - which is what separates this from the gaps above. The Drosophila null dies in the second instar and mouse loss of function is reported as causing neurodevelopmental defects and early lethality. Both are null phenotypes. No reported human patient is null: the severity range that defines this disorder lies entirely in the hypomorphic range, and neither organism has been studied at a hypomorphic dose.
Neither organism has the tissues the disease targets, either - a fly has no optic nerve or basal ganglia, and no mouse study reporting optic atrophy or basal-ganglia lesions on partial PTCD3 loss has been published. So the models establish that the gene is essential and say nothing about why partial loss produces this particular focal degeneration.
What would resolve it is a hypomorphic mammalian allele - a knock-in of one of the human leaky splice alleles, or a graded conditional knockdown - assessed for optic nerve and basal-ganglia pathology rather than for lethality.

selected_evidence.snippet: A loss-of-function mutant of PTCD3 is lethal during the second instar.

assertion.prompt: If an unaffected heterozygous carrier has the same reduced fibroblast basal respiration as her affected son, what does a reduced basal respiration rate actually establish in this disorder?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#Reduced Mitochondrial Respiratory Capacity and ATP Deficit
assertion.rationale:
In the 2024 report the mother of the adult proband - clinically unaffected, carrying one PTCD3 allele - had a basal respiration rate as low as her son's, with no significant difference between them. The authors draw the conclusion themselves: a lower oxygen consumption rate is seen in both affected and unaffected carriers, and that reduction is not by itself sufficient to cause disease.
The gap this leaves is a measurement gap. Basal respiration is being used as supporting functional evidence for variant classification in this gene, and in this family it did not discriminate patient from carrier. What has discriminated, in the two other functionally characterised families, is the complementation assay: subunit levels and maximal uncoupled capacity restored by wild-type PTCD3. Nobody has reported a maximal-capacity or complementation result on a heterozygous carrier, so it is not known whether those assays are any more discriminating.

selected_evidence.snippet: The similar results were observed in his unaffected mother, who is a carrier of the His269Tyr variant, concluding that both heterozygous unaffected and affected carriers exhibit a lower OCR.

assertion.prompt: Does the amount of residual PTCD3 protein explain why one genotype kills at 16 months and another allows independent survival into the fourth decade?
assertion.rationale:
The only proposed explanation for the disorder's enormous severity range is quantitative: the index patient's two truncating alleles leave PTCD3 nearly absent, while the leaky splice alleles of the later patients leave 15-30% of normal protein, and the 2024 authors extend the same reasoning to a missense allele. It is a plausible dose-response account and it is entirely uncontrolled - each level was measured in a different laboratory, in a different patient, with a different second allele, and nobody has plotted protein level against any severity measure.
What is missing is a graded series. Titrating PTCD3 in one cell background and measuring mitoribosome assembly, translation and respiration at each level would test whether the relationship is even monotonic. Until that exists the entry treats the residual-protein account as a hypothesis and does not use it for prognosis.

selected_evidence.snippet: As a result, the absence of PTCD3 protein is nearly complete, whereas in our patients, although reduced, was not absent.
